<STRUCT_0001>
Let us prove that this definition agrees with the definition in the
chapter on morphisms of schemes. This in particular guarantees that the
set of points where a morphism is <ACCENT_0001>tale is open.

Let <MATH_0001> be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let <MATH_0002> be locally of finite type.
Let <MATH_0003>. The morphism <MATH_0004> is <ACCENT_0001>tale at <MATH_0005> in
the sense of Definition <REF_0001>
if and only if it is <ACCENT_0002>tale at <MATH_0006> in
the sense of Morphisms, Definition <REF_0002>.

This follows from Lemma <REF_0001>
and the definitions.

<STRUCT_0001>
Here are some results on <ACCENT_0001>tale morphisms.
The formulations as given in this list apply only to
morphisms locally of finite type between locally Noetherian schemes.
In each case we give a reference to the general result as
proved earlier in the project, but in some cases one can
prove the result more easily in the Noetherian case.
Here is the list:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> An <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism is unramified. (Clear from our definitions.)
<STRUCT_0004> <ACCENT_0003>taleness is local on the source and the target in the Zariski
topology.
<STRUCT_0005> <ACCENT_0004>tale morphisms are stable under base change and composition.
See Morphisms, Lemmas <REF_0001>
and <REF_0002>.
<STRUCT_0006> <ACCENT_0005>tale morphisms of schemes are locally quasi-finite
and quasi-compact <ACCENT_0006>tale morphisms are quasi-finite. (This is
true because it holds for unramified morphisms as seen earlier.)
<STRUCT_0007> <ACCENT_0007>tale morphisms have relative dimension <MATH_0001>. See
Morphisms, Definition <REF_0003>
and
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0004>.
<STRUCT_0008> A morphism is <ACCENT_0008>tale if and only if it is flat and
all its fibres are <ACCENT_0009>tale. See
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0005>.
<STRUCT_0009> <ACCENT_0010>tale morphisms are open. This is true because an <ACCENT_0011>tale
morphism is flat, and Theorem <REF_0006>.
<STRUCT_0010> Let <MATH_0002> and <MATH_0003> be <ACCENT_0012>tale over a base scheme <MATH_0004>.
Any <MATH_0005>-morphism from <MATH_0006> to <MATH_0007> is <ACCENT_0013>tale.
See Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0007>.
